# Coverage matrix — 2026-10-14

**Which providers, in combination, make every value live.** Generated by
`npx tsx scripts/gen-coverage-matrix.ts` from two inputs, neither of which answers
the question alone: the source registry (`lib/data/dataSources.ts`), which knows
which providers *could* serve a surface and what each costs, and a live audit,
which knows what actually came back.

Audit: `http://localhost:3000` · mode **full** · run 2026-10-14T13:04:17.933Z
· 84 route probes (+6 cross-layer, which assert agreement
between layers rather than hitting a route) · registry: 56 surfaces

⚠ **IP-dependent.** The audit's verdicts depend on the egress it ran from, so this
matrix does too. Built from a cloud or CI run it describes that host, not a user.

## The number

| | |
|---|---|
| Surfaces in the registry | 56 |
| Live now, no key needed | **32** |
| Upstream throttled the audit — not a gap | 0 |
| Degraded — not serving the intended source | **19** |
| …of those, a key would fix | 12 |
| …of those, no key fixes | 7 |
| Not covered by any audit probe | 5 |
| Keyed provider entries behind them | 6 |
| **Accounts a user would open for full coverage** | **4** |

The account figure is a greedy set cover, so it is an **upper bound**. 3 of the
4 are forced — the only vendor that can serve some surface — and the
remainder were chosen most-surfaces-first. It counts accounts, not money: several have a
free tier, and the registry records `paid` separately from `key` for exactly that
reason. It also counts only what a key can buy — the unfixable rows below are a
product gap, and no number of accounts closes them.

## If we walk away from a vendor

Standing rule (owner, 2026-09-18): **decisions that cost money are deferred until
close to the end of production**, and the app is built so that no single provider is
load-bearing. This table is how that rule is checked. "Strands" is what would have
no remaining option at all if that vendor were dropped — the number to drive to zero.

| Vendor | Cost posture | Could serve | Strands if dropped |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Alpha Vantage** | free signup | 5 | — none |
| **FMP** | free signup · paid tier **deferred** | 9 | **3**: stock-universe, fund-holdings, options-calculator |
| **Finnhub** | free signup | 5 | — none |
| **LunarCrush** | free signup | 1 | — none |
| **Santiment** | free signup | 1 | — none |
| **Tiingo** | free signup | 5 | — none |
| **Tronscan API (TRON)** | free signup | 1 | **1**: wallet |
| **Twelve Data** | free signup | 6 | — none |
| **YouTube Data API** | free signup | 1 | **1**: videos |

### Single-sourced surfaces — the optionality risk

Exactly one vendor can serve each of these. They are where the rule is not yet
satisfied: dropping that vendor does not degrade the surface, it removes it.

- **Videos / video search** (`videos`) — only YouTube Data API (free signup)
- **On-chain wallet balances (BTC/ETH/SOL/TRON/XRP + EVM)** (`wallet`) — only Tronscan API (TRON) (free signup)
- **Stock Registry universe** (`stock-universe`) — only FMP (free signup · paid tier **deferred**)
- **ETF / fund holdings** (`fund-holdings`) — only FMP (free signup · paid tier **deferred**)
- **Options Calculator (payoff, breakevens, Greeks)** (`options-calculator`) — only FMP (free signup · paid tier **deferred**)

### Blocked only by a deferred paid decision

Every option here costs money and none is held, so under the standing rule these
stay as they are until late production. They are not defects to chase now.

- **Stock Registry universe** (`stock-universe`) — FMP
- **ETF / fund holdings** (`fund-holdings`) — FMP
- **Options Calculator (payoff, breakevens, Greeks)** (`options-calculator`) — FMP

### The ones no account closes

Every provider on these entries is keyless, and the keyless providers already ran
in this audit. So the gap is a geo-block, a withdrawn source, a terms decision or a
genuine absence — not a price. These are the rows that decide what "every value
live" can even mean.

- **Crypto OHLCV / candlestick charts** (`ohlcv`, UNCONFIGURED) — providers: CoinGecko (primary/none), DefiLlama (primary/none), Coin Metrics Community Data (fallback/none)
  - `/live-data/ohlcv?id=eth&range=MAX` → UNCONFIGURED — CoinGecko’s free service refuses candles past 365 days; a paid key reaches them, and the charts read DefiLlama closes
  - registry note: Candles from CoinGecko, closing prices from DefiLlama (T-423, D103), and from Coin Metrics’ Community API when DefiLlama does not answer a daily or weekly range (T-434, D108), credited on the responses it served (CC BY-NC 4.0); `source=coinmetrics` asks for it alone, which the audit does. CoinGecko’s free service serves no history older than 365 days and sends 4-day candles past 30 days. DefiLlama answers only callers that compute from closes and ask for them (`closes=1`: the Coins screener, Cycle Context, the Crypto Scanner and the multi-timeframe grid, which run only the setups and signal votes that read a close; the TA and coin-page charts where candles are missing or 4-day, drawn as a line; and the assistant’s price history where candles are refused, which then reports the highest and lowest close), marked `bars: "close"`; it carries no high, low or volume. Binance and Binance.US were the first candle rungs until 2026-10-13 (T-423, D102). `granularity` is measured from the candles.
- **Perp funding rates + open interest** (`funding-rates`, UNCONFIGURED) — providers: None — no source cleared for this use (primary/none)
  - `/live-data/funding-rates` → UNCONFIGURED — no source by decision (D40): No source: OKX, the only one, was withdrawn on 2026-09-30 because its API terms bar using its market data in an analytics platform. No other funding-rate source has been cleared for this use.
  - registry note: OKX was the only source and was withdrawn on terms grounds 2026-09-30 (owner decision D40): its API Agreement §9.4 limits Market Data — funding rates included, public endpoints expressly — to "your own personal, non-commercial trading and account management purposes" and bars using it in any "analytics platform". Binance futures (fapi) answers 451 from US hosts. The route answers ok:false with the reason, and the Market Structure panel shows funding and open interest as not available.
- **Staking APR/APY** (`staking-rates`, FALLBACK) — providers: DefiLlama Yields (aggregator/none), Lido (primary/none), Rocket Pool (primary/none), Marinade (primary/none), Jito (primary/none), Injective LCD (chain inflation) (primary/none)
  - `/live-data/staking-rates` → FALLBACK — 23/48 live APRs; 5/6 upstreams healthy — injective-native: http 502
  - registry note: Liquid-staking/restaking protocols + native network rates are live (DefiLlama + protocol APIs + chain inflation). CeFi exchange rates are static estimates. Each rate carries sources[key] = "live" | "estimate".
- **Crypto price chart (legacy, internal)** (`chart`, FALLBACK) — providers: CoinGecko (primary/none)
  - `/live-data/chart?id=btc&days=30` → FALLBACK — 721 price points, correctly marked synthetic:true (not real OHLC)
  - registry note: Synthesises zero-range OHLC from a price-only series (marked synthetic:true). No app consumers — /live-data/ohlcv provides real candles.
- **Stock social sentiment** (`stock-social`, UNCONFIGURED) — providers: StockTwits (primary/none), Reddit (Atom/RSS) (primary/none)
  - `/live-data/stock-social?limit=80` → UNCONFIGURED — 30 signals (stocktwits=30); Reddit withheld — Reddit is not read: its robots.txt disallows this app's agent, and its API needs Reddit's approval, which is planned for after launch.
  - registry note: Reddit 403s from datacenter IPs without OAuth — expect StockTwits-heavy results server-side. Budget allocated round-robin so one active source still fills the limit.
- **Equity screener / outliers** (`stock-outliers`, FALLBACK) — providers: Derived from stock-universe (derived/none)
  - `/live-data/stock-outliers?min_mcap=2` → FALLBACK — only 66 evaluated across 7 sectors — screening the curated catalog, not the real universe
  - registry note: Sector z-scores over whatever universe stock-universe returns — inherits its narrowness on the catalog fallback.
- **Futures term structure (forward curve)** (`futures-curve`, UNCONFIGURED) — providers: None — no reachable source quotes dated contract months (primary/none)
  - `/live-data/futures-curve?slug=gold` → UNCONFIGURED — no source (Yahoo removed on terms, 2026-08-06): 8 contract months resolved, none priced
  - registry note: Dated contract months (CLZ26.NYM style) priced through Yahoo’s v8 chart API, verified 9/9 across NYMEX/COMEX/CBOT by the P2-O1 audit (2026-08-05). Yahoo was withdrawn on terms grounds 2026-08-06 and nothing else the app can reach quotes a dated month — FMP/Tiingo/Finnhub/Twelve Data/Alpha Vantage carry continuous front-months at best, exchange settlement files are licensed. The route resolves the contract months and returns ok:false with the reason; the card states it on-page. Front-month prices are unaffected.

## Registry surfaces no probe covered

Not a verdict — an absence of one. Either the audit has no test for the route, or
the entry's `route`/`covers` do not match any path the audit hits. Both are worth
knowing: an unprobed surface contributes nothing to the number above, so the
account count is computed over a smaller world than the registry describes.

- `coin-profile` — Coin project profile (website, description) (/live-data/coin-profile, status `live`)
- `global` — Global crypto aggregates (BTC dominance, total cap) (/live-data/global, status `live`)
- `brief` — AI Daily Brief (/api/agents/research, status `derived`)
- `coin-rating` — Measured-risk rating (coin pages) (/live-data/coin-rating, status `derived`)
- `stock-rating` — Measured-risk rating (stock pages) (/live-data/stock-rating, status `derived`)

## Probes that match no registry entry

The join's other direction, and usually a test outliving the route it tested. The
registry is regenerated when a route is cut; the audit's test list is hand-maintained,
so it is the half that goes stale — and a 404 from a route deleted on purpose reads
as a data failure to anyone scanning the summary. These contribute nothing to the
account count either way.
